summary.headline: Flat week: orders 851 (-0.5% WoW) and revenue $60,547 (-1.3% WoW), but revenue just cleared its weekly target as Q2 opens; YTD still behind at 93%.

points.what: Orders came in at 851, down 0.5% week on week, while revenue fell 1.3% to $60,547.
points.so_what: Both movements are small and leave the week close to the 8-week averages of 790 orders and $57,236 revenue.

points.what: Revenue reached 100.4% of the weekly target ($249 above), while orders landed at 95.0% of target, 45 orders short.
points.so_what: The first week of Q2 is ahead on revenue but behind on orders, so attainment rests on order value rather than volume.

points.what: Year on year, orders grew 51.4% and revenue 44.9%, both below the 75% growth the targets assume.
points.so_what: Growth remains positive but is not fast enough to close the year-to-date shortfall of $58,749.

points.what: New customer signups rose 9.7% week on week to 259 and are up 10.2% year on year.
points.so_what: Customer acquisition improved in a week when orders slipped, the one clearly positive movement of the week.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate is reported for the mature week of 16 Mar 2026 because the two most recent weeks are not yet mature.
points.so_what: Return behaviour for the reporting week cannot be judged yet, so read 9.3% as a two-week-old signal.

points.what: The cancellation rate rose 0.6 pp to 14.2% and is 2.1 pp above last year.
points.so_what: Each percentage point of cancellations is worth about $706 of weekly revenue.

points.what: Year-to-date revenue is 93.0% of target, and hitting the $3,888,802 full-year target needs $79,813 a week versus a recent 8-week run-rate of $57,975.
points.so_what: The required pace is well above the current pace, so the full-year target is a stretch at this run-rate.

points.what: Weekly revenue of $60,547 beat its $60,298 target by $249 (100.4%), while 851 orders fell 45 short of the 896 target (95.0%).
points.so_what: Next week's bar is 854 orders and $57,958 revenue.

points.what: QTD revenue is 100.4% of target, $249 ahead, with $823,539 still needed over 12 weeks to reach the $884,086 full-quarter target.
points.so_what: Q2 starts marginally ahead, but almost the entire quarter target is still outstanding.

points.what: YTD revenue of $776,104 is $58,749 behind the $834,853 target to date, at 93.0% attainment, with Jan, Feb and Mar all behind and only Apr MTD ahead.
points.so_what: The year needs $79,813 per week across the remaining 39 weeks against a recent run-rate of $57,975.

points.what: LATAM was the largest contributor to the order decline, down 11 orders (-9.0%) to 111, accounting for 275% of the total change.
points.so_what: The small net drop of 4 orders masks larger offsetting regional moves.

points.what: North America rose 7.4% to 202 orders, adding 14 orders, while EMEA was flat at 163 and APAC slipped 7 orders to 375.
points.so_what: North American gains offset most of the declines elsewhere, keeping total orders near last week's level.

points.what: By traffic source, Facebook fell 11 orders (-18.6%) to 48, the largest single contribution, while Search added 11 orders (+1.8%) to 609.
points.so_what: Search, at 71.6% of orders, moved in the opposite direction to the smaller paid sources.

points.what: AOV was $82.94, down 0.1% week on week and down 2.0% year on year from $84.61.
points.so_what: Order value is slightly weaker than a year ago, so revenue growth of 44.9% trails order growth of 51.4%.

points.what: The cancellation rate rose 0.6 pp to 14.2%, versus 12.1% a year ago.
points.so_what: At roughly $706 of revenue per percentage point, the year-on-year gap is a meaningful drag on gross revenue.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the mature week of 16 Mar 2026 was 9.3%, down 0.2 pp from the prior week and level with last year.
points.so_what: Return behaviour is stable, so order quality concerns sit with cancellations rather than returns.

points.what: New signups of 259 were up 9.7% week on week and 10.2% year on year, against orders down 0.5% week on week and up 51.4% year on year.
points.so_what: Order growth is running well ahead of signup growth year on year, so volume is leaning on existing customers.
